classification.difficultyReason: Translate the watering description into an annular sector, subtract the opening angle from 360 degrees, infer the inner radius from the watering width, and subtract the two sector areas.

inlines.text: A golf course has a sprinkler system that waters the grass in the shape of a sector, as shown.
A sprinkler is positioned at point
. The unwatered opening shown has an angle of
The section of grass that is watered is 4.5 m wide at all points.
Water can reach a maximum of 12 m from the sprinkler at
What is the area of grass that this sprinkler will water?
Round your answer to the nearest square metre.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 7 diagram below the prompt on the left
spec.description: A shaded annular region surrounds L except for a 100-degree opening above it. M and N are the outer and inner endpoints on the left radial boundary. MN is 4.5 m; the maximum radius is 12 m. A labelled arrow identifies the watered region.
spec.mathematics: Concentric outer and inner arcs have radius ratio 12:7.5. The unshaded wedge is 100 degrees, so the shaded annular sector occupies 260 degrees. Construction coordinates encode these relationships without adding student-visible derived measurements.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens appear. The derived inner radius, shaded angle and area remain in the answer.

answer.worked:
For the shaded region shown, subtract the inner sector from the outer sector.

$$\begin{align*}
\theta &= 360^\circ-100^\circ=260^\circ\\
r &= 12-4.5=7.5\ \mathrm{m}\\
A_1 &= \frac{260}{360}\pi(12)^2\\
A_2 &= \frac{260}{360}\pi(7.5)^2\\
A_{\text{Total}} &= A_1-A_2\\
A_{\text{Total}} &= \frac{260}{360}\pi(144-56.25)\\
A_{\text{Total}} &\approx 199\ \mathrm{m}^2
\end{align*}$$

Rounded to the nearest square metre.
